dedupe_keys.name: solshade terrain aware solar illumination model

description: Solshade is a Python toolkit for modelling solar illumination over terrain using digital elevation models, orbital geometry and terrain shadows. Its own repository, documentation and package listing describe a reusable workflow for a site or landscape and its selected times. Spatial coverage is the supplied elevation grid; temporal coverage is the date and period selected by the user. The repository states MIT. Solar estimates can inform photovoltaic siting or the exposure assumptions of infrastructure near mountains and steep terrain. A caveat is that terrain geometry does not capture all local shading by buildings or vegetation, and solar illumination is not electrical generation without weather, panel and system models. No matching catalogue or first-review draft was found. The JOSS page and own documentation were inspected; no elevation file was downloaded and no radiation calculation was run. The illumination time series can supply a solar-generation simulation or asset-exposure analysis, subject to local validation. No directly related catalogue record was established.
name: Solshade terrain-aware solar illumination model
notes: G5 G5-0735. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
